title: Seraphim of Sarov
hook: a Russian Orthodox hermit who greeted every visitor, my joy, Christ is risen

segments.voice: Yesterday, the inner light: George Fox and the silent meeting. Your line was that of God in everyone. Did you look for it in someone difficult? Day two hundred eighty, the end of the week.

Think about how you greet people. At the door, on the phone, at work. Hey. Hi. What's up. Usually it's automatic. Now imagine someone who greeted every single person who came to see him, rich or poor, sick or angry, a stranger or a sinner, the same way, every day of the year: bowing low, smiling, and saying, my joy, Christ is risen! Not just at Easter. In winter, in the middle of the week, to people he'd never met. That was an old monk in a forest in Russia, two hundred years ago. Today: Seraphim of Sarov.
screen: `HEY. HI. WHAT'S UP.` → `MY JOY, CHRIST IS RISEN!` → `EVERY DAY OF THE YEAR.`

segments.voice: Seraphim was born in the 1750s in the Russian town of Kursk and became a monk at the monastery of Sarov. After years in the community, he went to live alone in a small hut in the forest, praying, reading the Gospels, and working a little garden. Many stories are told about those years. People say he fed a wild bear from his hand. And tradition says that when robbers came, thinking he had money, he let them beat him nearly to death without resisting, and afterward asked that they not be punished. He recovered, bent over for the rest of his life. Then, after many years of silence, he opened his door. Crowds came. And every one of them heard the same greeting: my joy, Christ is risen! That's the Easter greeting of Orthodox Christians, when one person says Christ is risen and the other answers, truly he is risen. Seraphim said it all year round, as if every day were Easter and every visitor were his joy. He's remembered for a teaching that's often passed on in one line: acquire the spirit of peace, and thousands around you will be saved. The words vary in the telling, but the idea is clear. You can't argue or force people into peace. But a person who is truly at peace changes the room. People came to him anxious and left calm. In another famous conversation, he told a visitor that the true aim of the Christian life is to acquire the Holy Spirit. Not rules for their own sake. The Spirit, and peace with it. Look back at this week: Catherine's courage, the quiet Imitation, the castle, the dark night, the kitchen, the inner light, and now Seraphim. Each one, in a different way, was learning peace.
screen: `A HUT IN THE FOREST.` · `HE DID NOT RESIST.` · `EVERY DAY IS EASTER.` · `ACQUIRE THE SPIRIT OF PEACE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice. Settle, and breathe. Think of the next person you'll greet today. A family member, a coworker, the cashier. Picture them. Now picture greeting them as if they were a joy to you, just for a moment. Not fake. Just open. Notice what it does in you to see them that way. Let your own breathing slow. That's where peace starts. The bell holds the time.
Seraphim of Sarov. The Russian hermit who called everyone my joy, and taught that peace in one person spreads to many.
Your line: acquire peace. Today, greet someone warmly, more warmly than usual, as if they were a joy. Day two hundred eighty.

howItsDone: Orthodox Christians honor Seraphim as one of Russia's most beloved saints, and many greet each other with 'Christ is risen' through the Easter season, answering 'truly he is risen'.

original.note: Russian: my joy; Seraphim's greeting to every visitor.

trapdoor: what you thought: a hermit who hid from people.
what it means: a man who spent years in silence and came out able to greet everyone as a joy, and taught that peace spreads.
what a scholar hears: the Paschal greeting used all year; the conversation with Nicholas Motovilov on acquiring the Holy Spirit; and canonization in 1903.
